tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

content.text:
BMW'nin asi ruhu deyince akla oversteer, sol şerit, selektör ve DSC'yi kapatmak geliyor. Jüri BMW olduğu için isimleri Almanca ya da İngilizce, açıklamaları Türkçe yazdım.

## En güçlü adaylar

1. **DSC OFF** — BMW'cilerin ilk yaptığı şey denge kontrolünü kapatmak. Tagline: *"Traction control for your roadmap — switched off."* İroni de var: uygulama aslında her şeyi audit trail ile kayıt altına alıyor. Asi görünüyor ama içi disiplinli, tam BMW gibi.
2. **Lichthupe** — Otobanda arkadan gelip selektör yapmak demek. Tagline: *"Flash the competition out of the left lane."* Uygulama rakip analizi yaptığı için bu anlam tam oturuyor.
3. **Linke Spur** — "Sol şerit". BMW'ciler orada yaşar. *"Where successor requirements overtake."*
4. **Oversteer** — Arkadan itiş, kontrollü kayma. *"Controlled chaos for product decisions."* Hem asi hem de yaptığımız işin tarifi: veri kaosunu kontrollü bir önceliklendirmeye çeviriyoruz.

## Daha agresif olanlar

- **Kickdown** — Gaza sonuna kadar basmak. *"Floor it from feedback to requirements."*
- **Redline** — *"We take customer complaints to the limit."*
- **Launch Control** — Hem BMW özelliği hem de ürün lansmanına gönderme.
- **Hooligan** — M sahiplerinin gururla taşıdığı lakap.

## İroni ağırlıklı

- **Rebel with an Audit Trail** — "Rebel Without a Cause" filmine gönderme. Asi ama her hareketi kayıtlı.
- **Sideways & Accountable** — Yan yan gidiyoruz ama hesabını veriyoruz.

## Önerim

İsim olarak **DSC OFF**, tagline olarak *"Rebel with an Audit Trail"* derim. Logo bir BMW ekranındaki "DSC OFF" ikaz ışığı olabilir, kayan araba ikonuyla birlikte. Sunumda şöyle bir punchline çalışır: *"Spirit of an M car, discipline of a PM: the AI drifts, the human holds the wheel."* Bu da PM in the loop prensibini esprili şekilde anlatıyor.

İstersen birini seçip uygulamaya ve dokümanlara işleyebilirim.

content.text:
Evet, ona **Haifischnase** (İngilizcesi *shark nose*) deniyor: ön yüzün öne doğru eğik durması. Klasik 2002, E9, E24 ve M1'de vardı, Neue Klasse konseptleriyle geri döndü. Proje de tam bunu yapıyor, geçmişten öğrenip geleceğe uzanıyor. Ayrıca köpekbalığının asi ve agresif bir karakteri var.

## İsim önerileri

1. **Haifisch** — Hem Almanca köpekbalığı hem de Rammstein şarkısı, yani Alman asi ruhu da içinde. *"Born with a shark nose. Hunts for requirements."*
2. **Sharknose** — Direkt ve anlaşılır. *"Old nose, new class, sharp decisions."*
3. **Apex** — Çift anlamlı: *apex predator* (köpekbalığı) ve virajın apex noktası (pist). *"Hit the apex of every product decision."*
4. **Shark Tank** — Hackathon jürisine birebir gönderme. *"Requirements pitch, the PM decides."* Çok eğlenceli ama TV şovunun adı olduğu için logoda değil, sunumda espri olarak kullanmak daha güvenli.
5. **Jaws** — Tagline: *"You're gonna need a bigger backlog."* Sunumda çok güldürür.

## Logo fikri

- **Köpekbalığı burnu + ok:** Öne eğik ön yüzün yan profili tek bir keskin çizgi olarak çiziliyor ve bu çizgi aynı zamanda ileri bakan bir ok oluyor. "Geleceğe bakan ürün kararı" mesajını veriyor.
- **Yüzgeç böbrek:** İki böbrek ızgarasından birinin üstünden su yüzeyine çıkan bir köpekbalığı yüzgeci çıkıyor.
- **Renkler:** M çizgileri (açık mavi, lacivert, kırmızı) ince bir aksan olarak kullanılabilir, gerisi koyu ve sade kalır.

Bir uyarı: BMW yuvarlak logosunu (roundel) ya da M logosunu birebir kullanmayalım. Ticari marka sorunu olur ve resmi BMW ürünü gibi görünür. Göndermeyi siluet ve renklerle yapmak hem daha güvenli hem daha zekice.

## Önerim

İsim **Haifisch**, tagline *"Rebel with an Audit Trail"*, logo da ok şeklindeki köpekbalığı burnu. Sunumdaki kapanış cümlesi de *"We're gonna need a bigger backlog"* olabilir.

İstersen logoyu SVG olarak çizip uygulamanın header'ına ve favicon'una ekleyeyim. Hangi ismi seçtiğini söylemen yeterli.

content.text:
Anladım. Hikâye şu: BMW yeni konseptlerde tasarımda geçmişe dönüyor, ama gerçek dönüş ruha dönüş olmalı. Ruh da müşteriyi gerçekten dinlemekten geçiyor. Bu güçlü bir pitch.

Elimizde çok iyi bir tarihi koz da var. **1962'deki ilk Neue Klasse (BMW 1500)**, iflasın eşiğindeki BMW'yi kurtaran araba oldu. Bunu insanların gerçekten istediği bir sportif sedanı yaparak başardılar. Bugünkü Neue Klasse ismini oradan alıyor.

## İsim önerileri

1. **Neue Seele** ("Yeni Ruh") — Neue Klasse'ye doğrudan gönderme. *"New class needs an old soul."* Sunum mesajını tek kelimeyle veriyor.
2. **Freude am Zuhören** ("Dinleme Zevki") — *Freude am Fahren* sloganının ters çevrilmiş hali. *"Sheer Driving Pleasure starts with Sheer Listening Pleasure."* Hafif iğneleyici ve zekice.
3. **1962** — Kısa, gizemli ve sarkastik. *"The last time BMW really listened to its customers, it saved the company."* Jüri gülümser, biraz da yutkunur.
4. **Remember Who You Are** — Aslan Kral'da Mufasa'nın Simba'ya söylediği söz. Uygulamanın BMW'ye "kim olduğunu hatırla" demesi çok komik ve tam ruha dönüş mesajı. Sunumda bir slayt olarak harika olur.
5. **Haifisch** — Önceki fikir de hâlâ uyuyor, çünkü shark nose da bu geri dönüşün tasarım sembolü.

## Önerim

Bunları katmanlı kullanabiliriz:

- **İsim:** Neue Seele
- **Tagline:** *Freude am Zuhören*
- **Açılış slaytı:** *"1962: BMW listened to its customers and survived. 2026: let's do it again, this time with an audit trail."*
- **Kapanış:** *"Remember who you are."*
- **Logo:** Shark nose silüeti tek bir çizgi olarak çiziliyor, burun ucundan da ses dalgası ya da konuşma balonu çıkıyor. Anlamı "geçmişin tasarımı, müşterinin sesi". Roundel kullanmıyoruz, gönderme siluetle yapılıyor.

Seçtiğin ismi söylersen logoyu SVG olarak çizip uygulamanın header'ına ve favicon'una ekleyebilirim. İsim değişikliğini de dokümanlara decision olarak işlerim.

message.content: ya shark nose logusu kullancam bir de bmwnin böbrek ile sıçıp batırmasını ama yeni conceptlerini beğnememi tasvir eden ve bu uygulama ile de aslında requirement projection yapmlaarını sağlicağım için ona uygun bir isim istiyorum

content.text:
Senin hikâyende üç şey var: böbrekler büyüdü ve iş batırıldı, yeni konseptlerle (shark nose, ince böbrekler) toparlanma geldi, uygulama da geleceğin requirement'larını öngörüyor. İsmin bu üçünü birleştirmesi lazım.

## En iyi adaylar

1. **SharkSight** — *Shark nose* ile *foresight*'ın birleşimi. Logoyla birebir uyuyor, öne eğik burun zaten "ileriye bakmak" demek. Requirement projection'ı doğrudan anlatıyor.
   - Tagline: *"Smaller kidneys. Sharper foresight."*
2. **Kidney Transplant** — En komik olanı. Dev böbrekleri söküp yerine müşterinin gerçekten istediğini takıyoruz.
   - Tagline: *"Replacing oversized kidneys with what customers actually asked for."*
3. **Grille Therapy** — BMW'nin böbrek travması için terapi. Gizli bir şaka da var: psikolojide de *projection* kavramı geçiyor.
   - Tagline: *"Recovering from the kidney years, one projected requirement at a time."*
4. **Dialysis** — Böbrek gibi süzüyor: 40 bin müşteri yorumunun içindeki gürültüyü ayıklayıp temiz requirement bırakıyor. Uygulamanın yaptığı işi tıbbi esprisiyle anlatıyor.
   - Tagline: *"We filter the feedback, so the kidneys don't have to grow."*
5. **Nose Forward** — Shark nose'un öne eğimi, geleceğe uzanmak demek.
   - Tagline: *"Learned from the kidneys. Leaning into the future."*

## Önerim

Ürün ismi **SharkSight** olsun, böbrek esprisi tagline ve sunumda yaşasın:

- **Logo:** Shark nose silüeti, burun ucu ileriyi gösteren bir ok gibi.
- **Tagline:** *"Smaller kidneys. Sharper foresight."*
- **Sunum akışı:**
  1. *"The kidney years"* (dev ızgaraların olduğu slayt, jüri güler)
  2. *"The comeback"* (Neue Klasse, shark nose geri döndü)
  3. *"What's next? Don't guess. Project it."* (SharkSight demosu)
- **Kapanış:** *"Next time, ask the customers before the kidneys grow."*

Böylece isim temiz ve profesyonel kalıyor, alay ise sunumda yapılıyor. Jüri BMW olduğu için bu denge önemli: isim BMW'yle dalga geçmiyor, sunum geçiyor.

İstersen SharkSight'ı uygulamaya işleyeyim: SVG logo, header, favicon ve dokümanlarda isim değişikliği.

## D-041 — Checkpoint lineage, comment galaxy and a new 3D frontend
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("design a black bg app with minimal design philosophy … graphic and 3D … make sure the second checkpoint will work on the output of checkpoint 1 and recalibrate requirements with the newly added data"; chose: comment galaxy as the first view, all BMW-internal data known at Jan, replace the old app, direction "track-while-scan"), implemented by agent · Status: accepted · Implements D-040; supersedes D-027's wave definitions and the D-039 screens.
- Decision:
  1. **Schema:** `checkpoint`, `checkpoint_run` (stage, parent_run_id), `track` (new/held/strengthened/weakened/lost with weight and prev_weight), `source_layout`; `source_item.checkpoint`. Module `bmw_req/checkpoints.py`: visibility rules, research import (`research/checkpoints/checkpoints.json` → `source_item(kind=research)`, 1,028 items), `start_run` refuses a cp2 run without a completed cp1 run of the same stage, `write_tracks` computes states against the parent and writes `lost` rows explicitly. Stage `acquire` run at both checkpoints (cp2: 6,645 held, 5,610 new). Tests: `tests/test_checkpoints.py`.
  2. **Galaxy:** all 10,128 raw comments embedded with text-embedding-3-small ($0.009) and laid out once in 3D (`bmw_req/pipeline/galaxy.py`); no AI interpretation of the text.
  3. **Frontend:** the D-039 screens and components are deleted; new app = checkpoint provider + sweep control + Scan screen (React + react-three-fiber, same stack). Colour encodes track state (blue = acquired by this sweep, white = held), not categories; isolation by car/market/channel/label/engine via the key.
- Consequences: the old API endpoints stay until the new screens replace them; their tests assume the 3-wave demo DB (3 fail on the current wave-1 DB, unrelated to this change). The calibration lab (`web/lab.html`, `web/src/three`) is kept.

## D-042 — One 5 Series; car rings carry dated public data
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("merge them into one 5 Series sector"; chose "add public July data" for the static rings), implemented by agent · Status: accepted
- Context: G68 has no comments and no own sales row (BMW's sheet is one G60_G68 tab); as its own car it was a near-empty sector. Study, options and sales rings never changed at JUL because BMW's files exist once (all known at JAN, D-041).
- Decision:
  1. **The 5 Series is one car line.** Requirements belong to the line; the China target is realised on the G68 (`market_variant`), US/EU on the G60. The G68 stays a separate vehicle in the data. On the scan: three car sectors; the last ~28 % of the 5 Series sector is the "LWB · China" part (G68 study items and sales, China research).
  2. **Car-specific public research goes onto the car's rings** (`api/routers/scan.py: research_cars / research_ring`): sales metrics → sales ring (stem = public volume), studies/reviews/awards → study ring, product news → options ring. They are contacts like the comments (dot = held, ring = acquired at JUL, flare when the sweep passes), drawn beside BMW's own marks and never blended with them (Q-015). The date ring keeps the remaining research and moved inside, next to the comments.
- Consequences: at JUL every ring gains items (public H1 2026 sales, J.D. Power 2026 IQS/APEAL awards, ADAC 2026, the 7 Series facelift and i7-China news). Matching is a regex on entity/headline; items naming BMW as a whole are matched by headline.

## D-043 — Structure & context: classify → cluster → contextualize → elicit, per checkpoint
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan (fresh extraction; evidence graph in SQLite with RAG; page 2 "collapse into structure"; "spawn sub agents to find optimizations … I want to see improvements with the new data"), designed from three read-only reviews (classification, clustering, contextualize), implemented by agent · Status: accepted
- Decision (code in `src/bmw_req/structure/`, every stage a `checkpoint_run`; cp2 builds on cp1):
  1. **classify** (`classify.py`, extract-v4): fixed ~45-aspect taxonomy shared by all sources (`taxonomy.py`); intensity (1–3) separate from impact; nature/want_kind/occupant/context/benchmark/future_cue/explicit; one signal per (aspect, nature); hints for Source C self-reported severity and the Source D survey prompt (never quoted); quotes ≥ 4 words; ~2.6k-token cacheable prompt; 20 comments per luna Flex call. cp2 classifies only the delta. A/B on a fixed 400-comment sample (`scripts/benchmark_classify.py`, `data/eval/classify_ab.json`): BMW-label macro 0.609 → 0.615, likes 0.84 → 0.90, "serious" → high 0.17 → 0.37, "minor" → low 0.22 → 0.49, quotes < 4 words 13 % → 5 %, survey-prompt quotes 10 → 0, Korea in-scope 0.71 → 0.76, aspect coverage 0 → 99 %; wants 0.56 → 0.54 (≈). `classify_context.py`: study rows (|z| ≥ 0.8 → gap/like), research (luna: aspect + nature), options (aspect) into `source_aspect`.
  2. **cluster** (`cluster.py`): portfolio-wide within polarity × category, average linkage 0.35 + recursive split of oversized clusters; stable keys `cl:<pol>:<cat>:<anchor>`; cp2 assigns new signals to cp1 clusters (mean-member cosine ≤ 0.35), clusters only leftovers; track weight = comment share, strengthened/weakened only if ≥ 10 % relative AND |z| ≥ 1.96 (the random JAN/JUL split must not look like change).
  3. **contextualize** (`contextualize.py`): luna standardizes one insight per cluster (title, statement, need type, quality issue, product decision); duplicate judge on cosine ≥ 0.86 pairs; themes (average linkage 0.45 on statement embeddings, cp2 joins nearest cp1 theme ≥ 0.55); RAG: research/study/options embedded once (`node_embedding`), per theme top-k checkpoint-visible candidates verified by luna into typed `evidence_edge`s (supports, contradicts, competes_with, trend_for, available_as_option, context). cp2 re-runs only changed clusters/themes; clean ones carry their edges as held.
  4. **areas** (`areas.py`): this step structures, it does not draft requirements (Atahan: drafting proposals is the next step). sol groups the themes into 15–40 potential requirement areas (title, need, kind improve / keep / emerging, why now from the given evidence, ≤ 3 open questions for drafting); code adds comments, line × market coverage and evidence counts; quality-only themes form a separate quality list. cp2 keeps area keys, attaches new themes, records change notes; tracks significance-tested. `elicit.py` (candidate drafting with code checks: future horizon needs a dated trend edge, own-market evidence per target, cited ids from the theme's edges) is kept for the next step and not run here.
  5. **Page 2 "Structure"** (`/structure`, same canvas as the scan): comments morph into their clusters; cluster nodes (blue improve / white keep; dot held, ring new, double ring strengthened, amber weakened/lost), theme halos, requirement-area diamonds above their themes, evidence arcs to the exact ring items; stage funnel; live agent panel (stages, progress, feed of AI steps from the audit trail; comments flash as they are classified); inspectors for clusters (signals with quotes), themes (evidence by relation) and areas (need, why now, open questions, coverage); "What the AI found" on comments and research on page 1. API `api/routers/structure.py`.
- Consequences: the old pipeline (`pipeline/`, extract-v3, findings, requirements, linker) stays for history but the new screens read only D-043 tables. Q-021 (over-linking) and the D-038 defect rule are enforced in code here.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

# Scan — raw evidence space

Mode: Operate. Audience: the BMW PM (Atahan) and hackathon judges on a laptop/projector. Job: see every piece of raw evidence the system holds, as one space, at a checkpoint; switch Jan 26 → Jul 26 and see what the second sweep added. Constraints: localhost only (confidential comments), black only, near-textless, 3D-first; checkpoint 2 always builds on checkpoint 1 (tracks, not snapshots).

## Direction contract
THESIS: each checkpoint is a radar sweep over one fixed evidence space; the app shows what a sweep acquired and how every track changed. Refuses the sidebar-plus-chart-cards dashboard.
OWN-WORLD: true black scan volume, white contacts, one BMW blue for the sweep and PM marks, amber only for weakened/lost; hairline range rings; mark shape encodes state (ring new, dot held, double ring strengthened, cross lost); numerals are the main text, wide Mona Sans.
STORY: the PM sees all raw evidence as one space, sweeps to July, watches new contacts flare in, hovers one to read the customer's words, filters by car or market.
FIRST VIEWPORT: full-bleed 3D galaxy of ~10k comments in a slowly turning scan volume; top-left three readout numerals; bottom-right the JAN 26 / JUL 26 sweep control; left edge a thin car/market key; click opens a right-side sheet with the comment.
FORM: own list candidate 5 of 7, track-while-scan; seed 8f8f8a79. Signature interaction: switching checkpoint sends a sweep plane through the volume, contacts it passes light up.
FINISH: unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished; this build ends with the finish review, the verdict, DESIGN.md, and every shipping raster carrying its provenance

## Recorded adaptations (2026-10-11, after the first finish review)
- User-pinned: each raw data type has its own colour (comments blue, research orange, study aqua, options yellow, sales magenta; validated categorical palette on black). This replaces "white contacts"; track state stays in mark shape (dot = held, ring = acquired by this sweep), flare and hover go white, the lock reticle is white.
- User-pinned: no auto-rotation; the volume moves only when the PM drags it. The sweep plays once on arrival (JAN → JUL) when no checkpoint is in the URL.
- Strengthened / weakened / lost marks and amber do not apply to raw sources (they are only ever acquired); they appear from the clustering stage on, where `track` states change.
- Key keeps five dimensions (car, market, channel, BMW label, engine): the raw comments carry all five and the PM asked to see the raw data.
- Every ring element opens an inspector that names its layer and says in one line what the ring encodes (user request).
